Someone raised a similar question about Xbox 360 games over at /v/CoOpGaming, so I'll expand on my answer from there:

Xbox Live Arcade (downloadable) - very pick up and play

  • Battleblock Theater - 2-player co-op, online or local, cartoony style gameplay, puzzle solving with a focus on working together
  • Castle Crashers - 4-player co-op, online and local, cartoony style, basic RPG with a very basic level-up and item system.
  • 'Splosion Man - 4-player co-op, online or local, puzzle solving platformer using characters that have one ability - Explode.
  • Monaco, What's Yours is Mine - 4-player co-op, online or local, a top-view infiltration game that has you play as a variety of characters to pull off the perfect heist.

Disc Based - most of these have more of a storyline or time investment

  • Diablo 3 (Ultimate Evil Edition) - 4-player co-op, online and local, some of the best co-op gameplay, storyline, and characters. In-depth level up and loot system that's still very accessible for newcomers to the series. Great game to pull an all-nighter with a group of friends.
  • Lord of the Rings: War in the North - 3-player co-op (2-player local), online or local, a slightly more basic, third-person RPG that has a pretty good storyline and characters.
  • Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell: Conviction - 2 player co-op, online or local, great stealth game almost similar to Metal Gear Solid that allows two player co-op campaign and features some great banter between characters as you infiltrate and execute
  • Tom Clancy's H.A.W.X. - 4-player online, easy to play air combat game
  • Tom Clancy's Rainbow Six Vegas 2 - a little dated, but still a great "breach and clear" style game
  • Army of Two series - great banter, third person shooter with co-op campaign, for two players.

All of these are still good single-player games, but great games to invite a buddy over and play for a section of time without needing to commit to a longer gaming session. The XBLA games especially are pick-up and drop again, so I'd suggest them first over the disc based games.

Well currently Xbox 360 games are around 10 or so dollars. If you get them used, which is fine by me. So I got a lot of games last year, and they were pretty awesome. For the price I believe I got my money's worth.

I bought Red Dead Redemption, and nothing prepared me for how awesome that game is. Dead Space 1, 2 and 3, they're around 10 dollars each but, it's an amazing trilogy if you are into horror, survival games, but this is definately worth it. The Darkness 1 and 2. 2 is superior in every way, but I guess if you are going to play this, you should just get the first game. Remember Me, I got that game for 4 dollars used, and I got my money's worth with that one. It's a definite try as far as under the radar games.
I got all the Gears of War Games for under 10 dollars as well, but, well, it shows it's age I guess. The first one was just, what's going on here kinda game. The second was extremely long and got tedious and the 3rd just, well you might as well play this because you are already pretty deep in it. But the gameplay is pretty awesome once you get used to it. Prince of Persia, the CGI one, awesome game, just, beautiful. It really surprised me, even if it's heavily borrowed from other platformers and the same name game. I got that for 5 dollars as well. Worth it. Darksiders 2, well you get to play as Death, but it cost me a bit more than 10, and I honestly thought this game was going to be short, but it's suprisingly long, but, that's not really that great. Still it was fun while I played it. All 3 Batman games for the last gen consoles, in this case xbox 360, Asylum, City and Origins, but I guess Origins isn't that great, but it was still a fun game at least to me. You can get all 3 in a pack for around 20. Metal Gear Rising, pretty cool if you like ninjas, and it does get increasingly difficult as you go on to fight stronger enemies. Chronicles of Riddick, Assault on Dark Athena, awesome game, and it includes the old game Escape from Butcher Bay, they're both very good and fun games. Tomb Raider the reboot, and I was surprised that this had come out for the 360 when I thought it would be only next gen, and my god, I got my money's worth, that game was amazing. It was bloody and fun.

Lastly I think you should look into playing Alan Wake. It's very cheap as well, don't remember how much but around 10. And that game surprised me as well. The fighting system, if there was any was repeated but very effective for the kind of game you were playing. It's one of those games that tries to become more than a game, and a story, and that's what it is, a story.

Anyways, have fun trying out some games.
